# Cabin fire dynamics

Open **Physics Lab → Cabin fire dynamics**. Use **Cabin balance** to change crew, controller, fuel or heat transfer. **Flame and spread** estimates local conditions at a flame front. **Independent checks** contains solver comparisons and the neural-network release decision. A trajectory download preserves its units, assumptions, time step and plotted samples.

## Sealed cabin, atmosphere and crew

For volume V at 300 K, initial gas moles are PV/(RT). In a closed chamber a repeat unit CₐHᵦO𝒸 consumes a+b/4−c/2 O₂ molecules, producing a CO₂ and b/2 H₂O. The front advances at the prescribed speed until its strip, combustible mass allowance or oxygen limit is exhausted. Extinction ends that fire for the remainder of the run. The two-minute default consumes 72 g cellulose, moves 36 cm, releases 1,094.4 kJ, and ends at 32.753% O₂ and 0.972% CO₂. The original strip balance gives the same result. The oxygen-concentration cutoff and prescribed speed are scenario inputs. [Fuel net heats of combustion](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/TN/nbstechnicalnote1128.pdf)

The metabolic model uses NASA activity-specific O₂ consumption and CO₂ production in grams per person per minute. Sleep uses 0.37/0.44, nominal duty 0.59/0.69, and aerobic work 3.99/5.22. The scrubber removes CO₂ up to its flow and cumulative sorbent capacity. Oxygen make-up starts half a specified tolerance below setpoint, adds toward the target and respects its own rate and tank capacity. Breathing stops consuming oxygen that is unavailable, and the returned oxygen shortfall marks that boundary. The controller operates on oxygen fraction. A physiological atmosphere assessment would also need inspired partial pressures, accumulated contaminants and biomedical criteria. [NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document, Table 3-24](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210024855/downloads/BVAD_2.15.22-final.pdf#page=63)

The 24-hour test uses a rigid 12 m³ cabin at 101.325 kPa, starting at 21% O₂, with two nominal crew, oxygen and scrubber capacities of 4 kg and 5 kg, and processing capacities of 3 and 4 g/min. Oxygen remains between 20.9000% and 21.0000% in a target band of 20.8–21.2%. Crew consume 1,699.2 g O₂ and produce 1,987.2 g CO₂. The sample interval in the downloadable trace is coarser than the controller step. The acceptance range uses every integration step. Switching off support or reducing tank capacity exposes supply exhaustion.

For a dry initial atmosphere, oxygen partial pressure is total pressure times oxygen fraction. At 101.3 kPa/21%, it is 21.27 kPa. At 56.5 kPa/34%, it is 19.21 kPa. The nitrogen partial-pressure-to-suit-pressure ratio for a 29.6 kPa suit falls from about 2.70 to 1.26 across those scenarios. That ratio is a comparison aid. An EVA prebreathe procedure requires mission-specific physiological evidence. The same starting oxygen partial pressure can coexist with different oxygen fractions, total pressures and material fire behavior. [NASA exploration atmosphere working group](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20130013505)

## Heat, pressure and remote sensing

The gas sensible energy above a 300 K reference is the sum of species moles times constant molar heat capacities at fixed volume times the temperature rise. N₂, O₂, CO₂ and water vapor use 20.8, 21.0, 28.8 and 25.3 J/(mol·K). The optional He and Ar diluents use 1.5R. The model adds net chemical heat, crew heat and battery deposition, with battery energy and cutoff time enforced. Extracted gases carry their modeled sensible energy. It applies an exponential wall exchange step with fixed wall temperature and heat-transfer conductance. Pressure follows nRT/V. The residual is the difference between energy added and the sum of energy stored, exported with gas and transferred to walls. It checks numerical bookkeeping. Gas temperatures also depend on the assumed deposited fraction, wall properties, spatial mixing, and the omitted condensation and heat capacity variation.

With no wall loss, the imposed energy stays in the modeled cabin except for extracted gas. The browser uses 1 s steps for an active front and 15 s for long no-fire runs. A 24-hour fixed-wall result does not include transient wall storage, routing heat into equipment, or local flame temperature. The end time, fuel and heat inputs apply to the particular trajectory.

The separate two-compartment solver now accepts an initial remote concentration. For a closed connection between compartments, initial remote tracer of 20 mg/m³, 8 m³ remote volume and 15 L/s of clean air, its remote signal decays as 20 exp(−0.015t/8). At 300 s forward stepping at 0.2 s gives 11.39445 mg/m³, against the analytic 11.39566. The largest relative error is 0.01055%. The sensor experiment supports calibration and evaluation on separate uploaded traces. [Transport fit protocol](#report/transport-fit)

## Dissociating equilibrium and thermal spread

Cantera 3.2.0 computes gas-phase equilibrium at fixed enthalpy and pressure for 53 GRI-Mech 3.0 species. The solid does not appear in GRI-Mech. For one fuel repeat unit we form complete CO₂/H₂O/N₂ products at 300 K with the correct elemental inventory, add the fuel's net heat of combustion to their reference enthalpy, then re-equilibrate those products at HP. This permits dissociation into species such as CO, H₂ and radicals while retaining the specified bulk heat input. This is an adiabatic flame-zone estimate for stoichiometric oxygen/nitrogen oxidizer, independent of inert-helium and argon cabin cases. It omits pyrolysis kinetics, soot, local mixture fraction and heat loss. [Cantera equilibrium example](https://cantera.org/3.2/userguide/flame-temperature.html) · [GRI-Mech input](https://github.com/Cantera/cantera/blob/v3.2.0/data/gri30.yaml)

The lookup ships 84 temperatures spanning two fuels, oxygen from 10% to 40%, and pressure from 30 to 110 kPa. Bilinear interpolation at ten off-grid conditions agrees within 0.835% of direct equilibrium calls, below the 2% acceptance tolerance. The table includes the species file's SHA-256. Fresh off-grid solves check interpolation accuracy; they supply no flight measurements. Regenerate using Python with cantera==3.2.0 and `python scripts/build_master_equilibrium.py`.

### Helium and argon cabin comparisons

The Atmosphere designer uses separate dissociating-equilibrium tables for helium and argon. It adds neutral He from Cantera’s NASA gas thermochemistry file to the 53 GRI-Mech species, including Ar. For each inert gas and fuel, the calculation replaces nitrogen with that diluent mole for mole. It uses the same fuel net heat and 300 K reference as the nitrogen solver. Helium and argon have nearly equal molar heat capacities across this neutral-gas model, so their temperatures at equal oxygen mole fraction and pressure are often identical to the published precision. Their molar masses differ, which changes the predicted mass of cabin gas. A temperature estimate is local to the idealized flame zone. Measured specimen spread, heat loss and gas ionization require additional models or evidence.

**Acceptance passed.** Both fuels at seven oxygen fractions and six pressures give 168 temperatures rounded to 0.001 K. At five other oxygen–pressure pairs for each fuel and diluent, 20 direct Cantera solves check the browser’s bilinear interpolation. The maximum relative error was **1.78481%** against a 2% limit. It occurred for polyethylene at 12.2% oxygen and 35.1 kPa in both gases. A direct solve gave 2,098.122 K. The browser withholds estimates outside 10–40% oxygen or 30–110 kPa. This comparison measures interpolation error against the thermochemical solver. It supplies no measured flame-temperature validation.

With Python and `cantera==3.2.0`, run the following from the repository root. The verifier checks the SHA-256 of both source YAML files, reproduces all shipped nodes, checks the 20 independently recomputed references against their published test values, and enforces the interpolation tolerance. The optional `--inert-report FILE.json` argument saves the complete grids, direct temperatures and errors. The default command without flags continues to regenerate the nitrogen Physics Lab table.

```sh
python scripts/build_master_equilibrium.py --check-inert
node --test tests/master-materials.test.cjs
```

[Cantera neutral helium thermochemistry](https://github.com/Cantera/cantera/blob/v3.2.0/data/nasa_gas.yaml) · [GRI-Mech species including argon](https://github.com/Cantera/cantera/blob/v3.2.0/data/gri30.yaml)

For the master document's full-thickness thin-fuel convention, speed in m/s is (π/4)·k_g/(ρₛ cₛ d)·(T_f−T_v)/(T_v−T∞). NASA reports SIBAL fabric near 0.32 mm with area density 0.182 kg/m². This gives 573 kg/m³ for 0.3175 mm. The nominal heat capacity of 1,350 J/(kg·K), pyrolysis temperature of 600 K and emissivity of 0.8 are engineering assumptions. Cantera gives 0.04578 W/(m·K) for 21/79 O₂/N₂ at 600 K. The default conditional speed is 0.738 mm/s. Under NASA's radiative-extinction scaling a low-flow screening velocity is εσ(Tᵥ⁴−T∞⁴)/[ρ_g c_pg (T_f−Tᵥ)], using the local pressure, ideal-gas density at Tᵥ and assumed gas heat capacity of 1,050 J/(kg·K). At the default conditions this is 0.592 cm/s. Quenching, blowoff and unknown regime selections withhold the speed. An observed blowoff boundary requires flow and kinetics data. [NASA thin-fuel experiments, theory and properties](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210011385/downloads/TM-20210011385.pdf)

The opposed Saffire-I run used approximately 21.5% oxygen and 20 cm/s airflow. The conditional prediction is 0.748 mm/s against 1.3 mm/s. Fitting that one record gives a multiplier of 1.739. At 21.6% oxygen, the midpoint of the concurrent record, the fitted prediction becomes 1.303 mm/s against the measured 1.8 mm/s. Both calculations assume 101.325 kPa. These two directions reuse one specimen, and the formula omits directional and thermal-history effects. The raw estimate meets the roadmap's factor-of-ten scale test. Holding one direction out reveals a 0.497 mm/s miss even after calibration. No oxygen limit or lunar front speed follows from this comparison. [NASA Saffire-I conditions, PSI-98 rows 2–3](https://doi.org/10.60555/0t15-1z43) · [Measured propagation rates, slide 21](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20170008805/downloads/20170008805.pdf#page=21)

## Recurrent surrogate release decision

Two local PyTorch models trained on 640 exact sealed-strip runs with 60 steps at 2 s intervals. A separate 96-run validation set selects the best epoch. The untouched 160-run test set yields 9,600 errors. The 24-state liquid cell learns its input and recurrent weights through a positive, input-dependent decay rate. A 24-state tanh RNN trains on the same features, runs, optimizer, epoch budget and target. Both estimates use the same physical clipping at the oxygen cutoff. A nearest-training-trajectory baseline averages the four nearest normalized scenarios. The stronger table uses two known fuel stoichiometries, 17 initial oxygen values and 37 consumed-oxygen fractions. It bilinearly interpolates before applying the cutoff. Knowledge of the equations makes this a demanding and relevant comparator. [Liquid time-constant networks](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16936)

| Method | Mean absolute O₂ error (points) | 95th percentile | Worst |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Liquid cell, 1,513 trained parameters | 0.13849 | 0.54840 | 3.08042 |
| Plain recurrent network, 793 parameters | 0.16605 | 0.52403 | 2.48413 |
| Four nearest training curves | 0.19315 | 0.58773 | 3.86930 |
| Chemistry-informed interpolated table | 0.00070 | 0.00173 | 0.00187 |

The release rule requires the trained liquid candidate to beat the structured lookup on held-out mean absolute oxygen error. **The candidate was dropped.** These metrics measure imitation of the equations. They do not establish validity against measured cabin fires. Reproduce with CPU PyTorch 2.6, NumPy, Node, and `python scripts/train_master_surrogate.py`. The JS fixture generator calls the existing exact solver, splits by entire run and records the seeds. The signed lunar forecast is independent of these experiments.

## Independent FDS fire cases

NIST FDS 6.11.1 ran three offline calculations on an Apple-silicon native build of the tagged source. Each run used one MPI rank and one OpenMP thread. The two sealed cubic chambers have 8 m³ of dry air at 101.325 kPa and 300 K, Earth gravity, a 0.25 m² floor burner, and inert enclosing walls. Each methane pulse ramps from zero to the specified heat-release density over 2 s, holds until 20 s, returns to zero by 22 s, and finishes at 45 s. The low and high burners use 50 and 100 kW/m². The high burner also runs with 24³ rather than 16³ mesh cells. The stored device output is the volume mean of oxygen mole fraction at each solver-reported sample time. All three `.out` summaries report successful completion. [NIST FDS release](https://github.com/firemodels/fds/releases/tag/FDS-6.11.1) · [NIST technical and validation guides](https://pages.nist.gov/fds-smv/manuals.html)

The comparator integrates the *prescribed* burner curve using 50,000 kJ/kg methane and 0.016043 kg/mol, independently of FDS's realized heat-release output. One mole of methane supplied at the surface consumes two moles of oxygen and contributes a net one mole of gas to the enclosure when water remains vapor. The predicted oxygen fraction is (x₀n₀−2ξ)/(n₀+ξ). The calculation uses the FDS device's starting oxygen fraction, 0.20954574, and no subsequent oxygen readings. Comparison is on the 46 reported timestamps for each case.

| Peak / cubic mesh | Final FDS O₂ (%) | Final balance O₂ (%) | Maximum error (O₂ points) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12.5 kW / 16³ | 20.742669 | 20.742874 | 0.004615 |
| 25.0 kW / 16³ | 20.531488 | 20.531580 | 0.007276 |
| 25.0 kW / 24³ | 20.529809 | 20.531580 | 0.006690 |

Each maximum is below the chosen 0.25-point tolerance. With oxygen held constant, the maximum error would be 0.213 and 0.425 points on the original coarse cases. The weak-fire constant baseline also passes that absolute tolerance. The coarse-to-fine final value moves 0.001679 points. These three cases test imposed fuel consumption and cabin-average inventory. Small prescribed burners bypass solid pyrolysis. They supply no lunar flame-spread result, measured cabin validation or evidence of local detector performance.

The repository stores three FDS input decks, original device and heat-release CSVs, and completion metadata in `data/master-physics/fds/`. The browser download includes their SHA-256 hashes, decks, paired traces, actual heat-release rates and errors. Run `python scripts/check_master_fds.py` to recalculate the comparison from the archived files. With a local executable, `python scripts/check_master_fds.py --fds /absolute/path/to/fds` reruns each deck in an isolated directory before computing the comparison. This release used GNU Fortran 16, Open MPI 5.0.11 and the official FDS-6.11.1 source tarball with SHA-256 `f0a3493ea5f77b18ee5aae065ffb5c3677ae5cc0e1479b5aac22872b472dc417`. The release was built from `Build/ompi_gnu_osx` with `make -j6 -f ../makefile ompi_gnu_osx VPATH=../../Source COMP_FC=mpifort LFLAGS=`.
